subject: Your Sunday read: 25 Training Feedback Questions to Ask After a Workshop
heading: 25 Training Feedback Questions to Ask After a Workshop
preheader: One useful read, a couple of lessons, and something to try this week.
body:
Hi there,

Let’s spend a few minutes on one idea this Sunday. This week’s read is “25 Training Feedback Questions to Ask After a Workshop”.

Here are two things I’d take from it:

A good satisfaction score doesn’t tell you everything. Someone can enjoy a workshop and still need more practice. Use feedback to understand what landed and where people need help; don’t treat it as proof that they’ve learned the skill.

Timing matters, too. Right after a session, ask about the pace, instructions and examples. Give people time to try the skill before asking how it worked in real life. Those are two different conversations, and both are useful.

As you read, think about one thing you could try with your own audience. You don’t need to change everything at once. Start with the part that feels useful to you.

There’s more context and practical detail in the full post. Have a read, and see what you’d like to try:

https://unsaidbox.com/blog/training-feedback-questions-after-a-workshop

Enjoy your Sunday,
The UnsaidBox team
